chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, and Safwan, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman who is divorced by Khul'a has neither a dwelling for her nor expenses.

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman who receives Khul'a (divorce initiated by wife)

ai.seo_question: What are the financial and housing rights of a woman divorced by Khul'a in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in Khul'a, where the wife initiates the divorce often in exchange for returning her mahr, she forfeits the financial maintenance (nafaqah) and housing (sukna) typically granted during the iddah. This ruling distinguishes Khul'a from standard talaq, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the financial obligations are contingent upon the nature of the divorce agreement and the party initiating the separation. It underscores the principle that the husband's duty to provide for the wife is linked to his right of retention, which is effectively waived in Khul'a.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, and Safwan, from Rafa’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The woman divorced by Al-Khul’a, there is neither (a provision of) a dwelling for her nor expenses’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
women in al-Khul‘ do not have the right for maintenance and housing.’”
